tasks.brief:
Implementation constraints: synchronous file I/O under threading lock; use `json` and `os` modules; do not use external ORMs. 

Behavioral specification: Add `load_versioned_snapshot(validator=None) -> (list, int)` to `src/services/storage.py`. Under the existing threading lock, attempt to read and parse the primary snapshot file. If `validator` is provided, call it on the parsed object. If parsing fails (JSONDecodeError) or validation fails (ValueError/ValidationError), move the corrupt file to a quarantine location (e.g., append `.quarantine`) and return `([], 0)`. If successful, return `(threads, revision)`. Ensure `save_versioned_snapshot` increments revision and writes atomically.

Acceptance condition: `grep -q 'def load_versioned_snapshot(validator' src/services/storage.py` succeeds. Valid JSON with invalid schema is quarantined and returns empty list/zero revision.

Implementation constraints: FastAPI route handler; synchronous service calls; use Pydantic models from existing imports; do not use async/await for service layer.

Behavioral specification: Modify `GET /api/v1/threads` in `src/api/threads.py`. Call `load_versioned_snapshot` passing the `ThreadSnapshot` model validator. Unpack `(threads, revision)`. Derive `quarantined` strictly from `bool(quarantine_files())` (checking for existence of quarantine files), NOT from the return value of `load_versioned_snapshot`. Return `ThreadsListResponse` with `threads`, `revision`, and `quarantined`. Ensure healthy empty storage returns `quarantined: false`. Implement PUT validation: reject invalid roles (422), reject malformed payloads (422, preserve stored), enforce revision preconditions (409 on stale, 422 on missing), and handle concurrent same-revision puts (one winner). Ensure each accepted PUT/DELETE advances revision.

Acceptance condition: `grep -q 'quarantined' src/api/threads.py && grep -q 'validator' src/api/threads.py` succeeds. GET returns quarantined=true only when quarantine files exist. PUT validates roles, payloads, and revisions correctly. DELETE clears snapshot and advances revision.

Implementation constraints: Vanilla JS; async/await for fetch; no external libraries; DOM manipulation via standard APIs.

Behavioral specification: Modify initial hydration in `src/static/app.js`. On failed GET `/api/v1/threads`, write exact text `history unavailable — retrying` to element `#history-status`. Retry the GET automatically (e.g., exponential backoff or fixed interval) until success. On success, install threads and revision into state before allowing any mutations. Clear the warning text from `#history-status`. Subsequent PUTs must adopt the revision from the response.

Acceptance condition: `grep -q 'history unavailable — retrying' src/static/app.js` succeeds. Hydration failure shows warning and retries; success clears warning and enables mutations.

Implementation constraints: Vanilla JS; async/await for fetch; no external libraries; DOM manipulation via standard APIs.

Behavioral specification: Modify thread deletion in `src/static/threads.js`. When a user confirms deletion of a single thread, remove it from the local state and enqueue a revisioned PUT to `/api/v1/threads` with the updated threads list and current revision. NEVER call DELETE `/api/v1/threads` for single-thread deletion. Ensure survivors persist through reload. Hydration status is owned by `app.js`.

Acceptance condition: No calls to DELETE `/api/v1/threads` in deletion path. Single thread deletion uses PUT with revision. Survivors persist after reload.
